title: spec-pack behaviors/order.json — derived implementation order
description: A projection of the inventory graph: which behaviors depend on which, and therefore what can be worked in parallel. Regenerated by c9 from nodes.jsonl/edges.jsonl and the COVERS edges; it must regenerate byte-identically. It holds NO mutable state — progress lives in behaviors/progress.jsonl, which this framework does not generate or validate.

generated_from.description: Hashes of the graph this order was derived from. If either changes, the order is stale and must be regenerated before it is trusted for scheduling.

dependency_edge_types.description: Which inventory edge types were treated as creating a dependency (default: INVOKES, READS, WRITES, RENDERS, STARTS, SCHEDULES). Recorded so the derivation is auditable rather than implicit.

depends_on.description: Behaviors that should exist before this one. Direct dependencies only — transitive ones are implied, not repeated.

evidence.description: The inventory edges that created this dependency, as '<from> -<TYPE>-> <to>'. A dependency with no evidence is an assertion, not a derivation.

wave.description: Longest-path depth in the condensed dependency graph. Every item in wave N can be worked concurrently once every wave below N is done. This is the parallelism the graph actually permits — not a schedule.

cycle_group.description: Non-null when this behavior sits in a dependency cycle. All members of a cycle share one group id and cannot be strictly ordered — they are implemented together, or a human breaks the cycle deliberately. Cycles are normal in legacy applications and are reported, never silently broken by the generator.

dependents_count.description: How many behaviors transitively depend on this one. High values are the highest-leverage work and the most expensive to get wrong — useful for ordering within a wave, which the graph itself does not determine.

waves.description: Convenience index: wave number to the behaviors in it. Derivable from items; materialized so a scheduler need not recompute it.

cycles.description: Every dependency cycle found, so they are visible in one place rather than discovered per-item.
